cards.a: A type of bonding and sequestration of metal atoms.

cards.q: What names are given to the ligand involved in chelation?
cards.a: Chelant, chelator, chelating agent, or sequestering agent.

cards.q: What bonding arrangement forms the ring structure in chelation?
cards.a: Two or more separate dative covalent bonds between a ligand and a single metal atom.

cards.q: Why is a crab's claw used as the metaphor for chelation?
cards.a: Because the ligand molecule or molecules hold the metal atom like the claws of a crab.

cards.q: How many chelate rings do ligands of higher denticity form?
What is chelation therapy used for?
cards.a: Removing toxic metals from the body.

cards.q: What does the Greek word χηλή (chēlē), the origin of "chelation", mean?

cards.a: Sir Gilbert T. Morgan and H. D. K. Drew.

cards.q: In what year was the term "chelate" first applied?
What type of chelate ring does ethylenediamine form when binding a metal?
In which medical imaging application is chelation useful?
cards.a: As contrast agents in MRI scanning.
